sections.title: Read the passage and fill in the blanks.

questions.q: Contemporary art in India began with the ______ rule.
Jamini Roy, Raja Ravi Varma and ______ Tagore were pioneers.
The artists struggled to retain Indian ______.
Experiments were done in print making: woodcut, lithograph and ______.
The Progressive Artists Group exhibited in ______.

sections.passage: Contemporary art began with the British rule in India. Raja Ravi Varma, Abanindranath Tagore, Amrita Shergil, Rabindranath Tagore and Jamini Roy were the pioneers of contemporary Indian art. These young artists were more exposed to western art movements. German Expressionism, Cubism, Fauvism, Dadaism and Surrealism left a great influence on them, but at the same time their struggle to retain Indian identity continued. A lot of experiments were done with print making such as woodcut, lithograph and etching. The Progressive Artists Group of Bombay exhibited the paintings of F.N. Souza, Raza, M.F. Hussain and K.H. Ara in 1947.

sections.passage: Benode Behari Mukherjee was a student of Nandalal Bose, the famous Bengal School painter. He loved nature and its beauty. He learnt the art of landscaping from Japan. He suffered from weak eyesight from childhood and became totally blind in the later part of his life. In spite of his blindness he created a huge mural at Kala Bhavan, Santiniketan. 'The Mediaeval Saints' is one of the murals which he painted on the wall of Hindi Bhavan in the Fresco Buono technique, in which powdered pigment colours are mixed in water and applied to wet freshly laid lime plaster ground. (April 2025)

sections.title: Read the passage and state whether each statement is true or false.

questions.q: Souza was born in Goa.
Souza settled in Paris after leaving India.
He was one of the founders of the Progressive Artists Group.
In 'Landscape in Red' the predominant colour is green.
questions.answer: False – red is predominant, with splashes of green.

sections.passage: Francis Newton Souza was born in Goa and grew up in Mumbai. He was expelled from the J.J. School of Art in 1945. He was one of the young painters who formed the Progressive Artists Group in 1947. Later he left India and settled in London. He protested against religious and social superstitions through his paintings. Like most of his contemporaries Souza was inspired by Post-Impressionist and German Expressionist painters, and he was greatly influenced by Picasso and Matisse. 'Landscape in Red' is an experimental cityscape in which red is the predominant colour. (October 2025)

sections.title: Read the passage and state whether each statement is true or false.

questions.q: Panikar was a pioneer of contemporary art in South India.
He established the artists' village Cholamandalam near Chennai.
'Words and Symbols' uses bright colours as the main element.
questions.answer: False – colours play a nominal role.

questions.q: Panikar used Roman and Malayalam scripts in the painting.

sections.passage: K.C.S. Panikar was the most influential pioneer in the development of the contemporary art movement in South India. He was a student of D.P. Roy Choudhury. His style went through many stages from realistic to geometric. He established the first artists' village of India near Chennai named Cholamandalam. 'Words and Symbols' is an experimental work in which space is covered with calligraphy. Panikar used mathematical symbols, Arabic figures, Roman and Malayalam scripts and Tantric symbolic diagrams. Colours play a nominal role.

questions.q: What do you know about the 'Progressive Artists Group'? Name a few artists of this group.
questions.answer: The Progressive Artists Group of Bombay was formed in 1947 and exhibited its paintings that year; its artists included F.N. Souza, S.H. Raza, M.F. Hussain and K.H. Ara. They took western influences while searching for an Indian identity.

questions.q: Explain the painting 'Landscape in Red'.
questions.answer: F.N. Souza's 'Landscape in Red' (oil, 1961) is an experimental cityscape showing a city as a concrete jungle with a mysterious character. Calligraphic lines are arranged with colours; red predominates with a few splashes of green; no rule of perspective is followed yet depth of space is clearly shown.

questions.q: Write a note on Francis Newton Souza.
questions.answer: Souza (1924–2002) was born in Goa and grew up in Mumbai; expelled from J.J. School of Art in 1945, he was a founder of the Progressive Artists Group in 1947 and later settled in London. He protested against superstitions, was influenced by Picasso and Matisse, combined Indian temple sculpture with western art and is compared with Picasso.

questions.q: What do you know about the Indian painter who became blind?
questions.answer: Benode Behari Mukherjee, a student of Nandalal Bose, had weak eyesight from childhood and became totally blind later but still created a huge mural at Kala Bhavan, Santiniketan, including 'The Mediaeval Saints' in Fresco Buono at Hindi Bhavan.

questions.q: What is Graphics or print making? Name some of the print making techniques.
questions.answer: Graphics or print making is an art form in which a number of copies of the same picture are produced. Techniques include etching, dry point, aquatint, intaglio, lithography and oleography.

questions.q: Describe Panikar's painting 'Words and Symbols'.
questions.answer: It is an oil painting on board (1965) from his series 'Words' and 'Symbols': space is covered with calligraphy of mathematical symbols, Arabic figures, Roman and Malayalam scripts and Tantric diagrams, looking like a horoscope, with colour playing a nominal role.

questions.q: Define Fresco Buono.
questions.answer: Fresco Buono is a method of wall painting in which powdered pigment colours mixed in water are applied to wet, freshly laid lime plaster so that the colour becomes part of the wall and lasts long.

questions.q: State the methods and techniques used by contemporary artists of India.
questions.answer: They combined western techniques with Indian spiritualism, used far-eastern (Japanese and Chinese) methods, and experimented a great deal with print making (woodcut, lithograph, etching, intaglio) and with folk art and murals.

sections.title: Short answer question. Answer in 50–60 words.

questions.q: Describe the technique and message of Krishna Reddy's 'Whirlpool'.
questions.answer: 'Whirlpool' (1962, intaglio on paper) is made by incising the design lines in a copper or zinc plate; ink is held only in the furrows, the surface is wiped clean, damp paper is laid on it and the print is taken under pressure. Reddy creates abstract forms from stars, flowers and clouds to capture the force of nature: everything is lost in the cosmic whirlpool. His early training in sculpture gives the relief-like intaglio effect.

questions.q: Describe the mural 'The Mediaeval Saints'.
questions.answer: Painted by Benode Behari Mukherjee in 1947 on the wall of Hindi Bhavan, Visva-Bharati, in Fresco Buono, it shows saints of different religions as huge elongated figures arranged in flowing, river-like movement with a monument-like quality like Gothic sculpture; the emphatic verticality is balanced by smaller figures in horizontal continuity showing common people. The lines are emphatic and the colours limited to brown, yellow ochre and terraverte.

questions.q: Write about two painters of India who settled abroad and became famous.
questions.answer: F.N. Souza settled in London and also lived in New York; he became one of the top five artists to represent India internationally, with works like 'Landscape in Red'. Krishna Reddy, a Santiniketan-trained print maker, became famous for intaglio prints like 'Whirlpool'.
questions.note: The textbook names Souza's London and New York stays; Krishna Reddy's work is described under 'Whirlpool'.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 70–80 words.

questions.q: Describe the influences that helped in the development of contemporary art of India.
questions.answer: Contemporary art began with British rule. Indian artists were exposed to German Expressionism, Cubism, Fauvism, Dadaism and Surrealism, yet struggled to keep their Indian identity; a combination of western technique and Indian spirituality became its essence. They also used far-eastern methods, experimented with print making (woodcut, lithography, etching), folk art and Japanese art, and groups such as the Calcutta Group (1943) and the Progressive Artists Group (1947) formed. Teachers like Roy Chowdhury, Saroda Ukil and Panikar spread the movement in the north and south; some artists settled abroad.

questions.q: Describe in brief one famous painting of Panikar or Souza.
questions.answer: K.C.S. Panikar's 'Words and Symbols' (1965, oil on board) covers space with calligraphy of mathematical symbols, Arabic figures, Roman and Malayalam scripts and Tantric diagrams that look like a horoscope; colour plays a nominal role. F.N. Souza's 'Landscape in Red' (1961, oil) is an experimental cityscape of a concrete jungle with red predominating and splashes of green; calligraphic lines are used and no perspective is followed, yet depth of space is clear.

questions.q: Write a note on Benode Behari Mukherjee and his mural 'The Mediaeval Saints'.
questions.answer: Benode Behari Mukherjee (1904–80), a student of Nandalal Bose, loved nature, learnt landscape from Japan and used simple calligraphic lines. Weak-eyed since childhood and finally blind, he still created a huge mural at Kala Bhavan. 'The Mediaeval Saints' (1947) on the wall of Hindi Bhavan, Visva-Bharati, is a Fresco Buono wall painting of saints of different religions as huge elongated figures in flowing rhythm, balanced by smaller figures of common people, in brown, yellow ochre and terraverte.
